# Fairstay Eligibility Checks (`fairstay-eligibility-checks`)

Checks eligibility for every nursing-home resident in the building: missing or stale checks, inactive or ended coverage still on the census, coverage ending soon, Medicare Part A benefit days running out, missing or short qualifying hospital stays, admissions more than 30 days after the hospital, and Medicaid renewals due. Resident identifiers are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay Eligibility Checks never logs in to payer or state portals; staff run the checks.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Billing and revenue cycle · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-eligibility-checks demo
npx -y fairstay-eligibility-checks mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional: Riverbend Care Center residents and made-up payers marked "(fictional)". As of 2026-03-02 the planted problems are: Part A days running out (R202: 12 earlier days + 83 this stay), a 2-day qualifying stay, a late admission and a stale check (R203), Medicaid coverage that ended but is still on the census and a renewal due (R204), a "Not eligible" result (R205), managed care coverage ending (R206, waiver recorded), and no eligibility check at all (R209). A discharged resident (R208) and a private-pay resident (R207) are skipped.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `eligibility_check` | List eligibility problems for the residents in the building on as_of, most urgent first. | runs |
| `eligibility_write_report` | Write eligibility.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and eligibility.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/eligibility). | runs |
| `eligibility_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `eligibility_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `eligibility_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `eligibility_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `eligibility_portal_login` | Fairstay Eligibility Checks never logs in to payer or state portals; staff run the checks. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `eligibility_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `census` (required) | Census export under --root: residents, payer and dates (the residents in the building on as_of are checked) |
| `eligibility` (required) | Eligibility results under --root: resident, payer, status, date checked, coverage dates, Part A days used, Medicaid renewal date |
| `stays` | Optional hospital stays under --root: resident, hospital admit and discharge, SNF admit, waiver |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: stale_days, warn_days, renewal_warn_days |
| `as_of` | Date to check on (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-eligibility-checks inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Census (`census`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `facility` | text | Facility, Facility Name, Building, Location, Fac, Center |
| `from` (required) | date | From, Start, Start Date, Effective Date, Begin Date, From Date, Admit Date, Census Date |
| `to` | date | To, End, End Date, Thru, Through, Thru Date, Through Date, To Date |
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `payer_type` | text | Payer Type, Payor Type, Payer Class, Payer Category, Pay Type |
| `level` | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |
| `bed_status` | text | Bed Status, Status, Census Status, Action, Census Action, Leave Type |
| `room` | text | Room, Room Bed, Bed, Room/Bed, Unit |

## Settings file (`eligibility_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `stale_days` | A check older than this many days is stale (default 30) |
| `warn_days` | Warn this many days before coverage or Part A days run out (default 14) |
| `renewal_warn_days` | Warn this many days before a Medicaid renewal (default 60) |

## Memory

`eligibility_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `eligibility_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `qualifying_stay_waiver` | notes the waiver on that payer's residents in results. Part A residents are still checked; it never removes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-eligibility-checks": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-eligibility-checks",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-eligibility-checks -- npx -y fairstay-eligibility-checks mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-eligibility-checks tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-eligibility-checks sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-eligibility-checks inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-eligibility-checks call eligibility_check '{"census":"<census>","eligibility":"<eligibility>"}'
fairstay-eligibility-checks eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-eligibility-checks demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
